generatedFrom: 2026-10-22 D10 re-verification: the visibility dialog/delete preview already implement host-scoped targets, scan locking, acceptance predicates, virtualized recovery and the host-aware error copy

rows.note: The confirmed row resolves by id+host, the dialog closes with the stale notice when nothing resolves, and App clears the target state on close.
Batch rows print the host label when a path collides; single vs batch previews use region/list semantics.
The review action guards non-git projects and passes the repo's execution host; the dialog resolves the target by repo+host.
Open runs an authoritative scan with checking/ready/failed; an active mutation skips it; every source action locks while checking.
Show-by-path is fenced by scope, clears the row locally and re-scans; success leaves listState ready.
Show/Hide ships the update with an isAccepted predicate evaluated against the latest repo row.
Use global only appears when the override matches the global value, and the commit carries an acceptance predicate.
Adding a custom root validates limit/absolute/duplicate and accepts only when the source and its 'hide' preference land in the latest row.
Removing a custom root accepts only when the source and its preference are gone, leaving the other preferences intact.
Above ten rows the recovery list virtualizes with react-window; each action is named 'Show <branch> at <path>'.
Actions disable for checking/busy/toggling, and Manage in Global Settings sits below the source list.
The segment group is named with the full custom rootPath; re-selecting the active segment still writes a full replace.
Keep-hidden failures publish 'Could not keep external worktrees hidden. Try again.' on the row's alert and clear on success.
One shared 1s interval for every subscriber, with subscribe/unsubscribe, stopClock and an immediate currentNow publish.
getLatestRepoForVisibilityScope resolves the current repo row for the host-qualified scope.
Every source mutation carries its isAccepted predicate.
A dropped preference from the target host maps to the dedicated 'This host doesn't support source-specific worktree visibility' copy.
Picking the global value is detected inline (matchingOverride) and routed to the revert mutation with acceptance.
